subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr had his pocket cleanly picked by Mari and is seeking an opportunity to leave, but decides to explore the village after being egged on by Calmer's disrespectful tone.
source_quote: Let’s go explore the village and see if we can learn anything!

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer drinks the last of his mead and responds to Zephyr with the most disrespectful tone he can muster, saying, “As you wish, boss!”
source_quote: As you wish, boss!

subject: Sheernobb
fact: Sheernobb is a small town dominated by the Moot Hall, with roads splitting into two branches — one north and one south — that converge after the hall, forming a circular route around which most stores are located.
source_quote: The village of Sheernobb is a small town. The dominant building is what the locals call the Moot Hall... The two branches converge after the moot hall on the road going out of town.

subject: Moot Hall
fact: The Moot Hall is the central building in Sheernobb, located on the largest hill, with wide stone steps leading to grand carved doors opening into the Feasting Hall, used for special gatherings.
source_quote: The Moothall is in the center of Sheernobb on the largest hill. It boasts wide stone steps leading to grand stone doors carved with runes. These doors open into the Feasting Hall...

subject: Grindin Books
fact: Grindin Books is a dimly-lit bookshop housed in a small cottage, instantly recognizable by its cluttered display of books and maps in the windows and a studded oak door bearing the sign, “Welcome to the Grindin Books.”
source_quote: Nestled within a small cottage, Grindin Books is instantly recognizable by the cluttered display of books and maps in its windows and a studded oak door bearing the welcoming sign, “Welcome to the Grindin Books.”

subject: Grindin Well-Read
fact: Grindin Well-Read is a gnome bookkeeper who sits behind a counter in a plush reclining chair, with green-tinted candles positioned for comfortable reading. He is annoyed by intrusions and claims his invitation to a conference was stolen, not that he lacks merchandise.
source_quote: My invitation to the conference was stolen! I didn’t have the opportunity to reject the invitation!

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia, a spy, observes Grindin Well-Read and concludes that low-value merchants like booksellers are often the most well-connected. He is frustrated by Grindin’s distraction but learns that Palsmarie Clee has information on the bandits.
source_quote: Another ignorant fool.

subject: Map of the Elemental Nexus
fact: A book titled 'Map of the Elemental Nexus' is visible in Grindin Books. Zinnia recognizes its potential value for understanding the elemental planes.
source_quote: His eyes catch the title of a book - Map of the Elemental Nexus.

subject: Tavern
fact: The Tavern is located on the southern branch of the road, just after the road into town ends.
source_quote: The Tavern is on the south branch, just after the road coming into town ends.

subject: Bookstore Branch
fact: The northern branch of the road leads to the bookstore, Grindin Books, which is the destination Zephyr ultimately chooses after initially considering the southern route.
source_quote: Zephyr remembers how a bookstore was on the northern branch.

subject: Djinibac’s Apothecary
fact: Djinibac’s Apothecary is one of the stores located along the southern branch of the road in Sheernobb.
source_quote: He notes the stores: “Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.”

subject: Tabac Shop
fact: The Tabac Shop is one of the stores located along the southern branch of the road in Sheernobb.
source_quote: He notes the stores: “Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.”

subject: Fiver Woodcarver
fact: Fiver Woodcarver is one of the stores located along the southern branch of the road in Sheernobb.
source_quote: He notes the stores: “Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.”

subject: Peony’s Mill
fact: Peony’s Mill is one of the stores located along the southern branch of the road in Sheernobb.
source_quote: He notes the stores: “Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.”

subject: Henker’s Shop
fact: Henker’s Shop is one of the stores located along the southern branch of the road in Sheernobb, near a pond.
source_quote: He notes the stores: “Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.”

subject: Naglo Crystal Divine Shop
fact: Naglo Crystal Divine Shop is one of the stores located along the southern branch of the road in Sheernobb.
source_quote: He notes the stores: “Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.”

subject: Pond
fact: A pond is located near Henker’s Shop along the southern branch of the road in Sheernobb.
source_quote: He notes the stores: “Djinibac’s Apothecary, a Tabac Shop, Fiver Woodcarver, Peony’s Mill, and would you look at that a pond, Henker’s Shop, Naglo Crystal Divine Shop, and there is Grindin Books.”

subject: Feasting Hall
fact: The Feasting Hall is the largest building in Sheernobb, accessed through the Moot Hall’s grand stone doors, and used for special gatherings.
source_quote: These doors open into the Feasting Hall, the village’s largest building, used for special gatherings.

subject: Statue of Keenleene
fact: A statue of Keenleene, Founder of Sheernobb, stands just before the entrance to the Moot Hall. It is made of ancient grey stone and comes to life with illusionary mischief.
source_quote: Just before the entrance is a statue. Sequoia wants to look at it and approaches. At the statue's base, he reads a sign - “Keenleene, Founder of Sheernobb!”

subject: Keenleene
fact: Keenleene is an illusionary gnome spirit who manifests from his statue, laughing heartily, playing pipes, and winking at observers. He brings an undeniable sense of happiness and mirth.
source_quote: Before his eyes, the stone figure of Keenleene transforms, coming to life with lifelike mischief... He picks up his pipes and starts playing a lively tune...

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia, a halfling, observes Keenleene’s illusion and concludes that gnomes are master illusionists who love putting on shows, prompting the group to proceed to the Moot Hall.
source_quote: Gnomes are master illusionists. And they love to put on shows like this.

subject: Moot Hall Doors
fact: The grand stone doors of the Moot Hall are carved with runes reading 'Ni te pharkalu, quo lun verra lu,' which translates to 'If you see it, it’s not the right it.'
source_quote: These doors open into the Feasting Hall... with runes carved over the door — Ni te pharkalu, quo lun verra lu, with a helpful translation in common: “If you see it, it’s not the right it.”

subject: Palsmarie Clee
fact: Grindin Well-Read confirms that Palsmarie Clee has information on the bandits, providing a critical lead for Zinnia’s investigation.
source_quote: Grindin finally confirms that Palsmarie Clee has information on the bandits.

subject: Stolen Conference Invitation
fact: Grindin Well-Read claims his invitation to a conference was stolen, suggesting a possible link between high-profile disappearances and bandit activity in the region.
source_quote: My invitation to the conference was stolen! I didn’t have the opportunity to reject the invitation!

subject: Enchanted Wards for Caravans
fact: Grindin Well-Read suggests employing enchanted wards and protective charms to deter bandit attacks, implying awareness of broader security failures in the region.
source_quote: Enchanted wards and protective charms could be distributed to caravans to deter bandit attacks.

subject: Keenleene’s Illusion
fact: The statue of Keenleene activates as an illusion, bringing laughter, music, and joy to all who witness it — an event that distracts but also reveals the town’s deep ties to gnomish magic.
source_quote: The enchantment brings an undeniable sense of happiness and amusement, captivating.

subject: Gnomes of Sheernobb
fact: Gnomes are recognized as master illusionists in Sheernobb, known for elaborate public performances and magical displays, as exemplified by Keenleene and Grindin Well-Read.
source_quote: Gnomes are master illusionists. And they love to put on shows like this.

subject: Planting 21, 579 Early Afternoon
fact: All events occur on Planting 21, 579, in the early afternoon, marking a single day of investigation and discovery in Sheernobb.
source_quote: Planting 21, 579 Early Afternoon

subject: Glennddarc
fact: Glennddarc is the Headgnome of Sheernobb, a village in the Kron Hills. He is weary of petty concerns like bandits and is focused on the threat of giants. He is currently asleep in an elegantly engraved oak chair, barefoot and crossed at the ankles over one arm. He is romantically intrigued by Pasmarie Clee and believes Gnonsbim is pursuing her for political gain.
source_quote: If you ask me, Gnonsbim has gone sweet on her. If you want to help a young gnome looking for a wife, listen to Gnonsbim. When you want to help the town, I need help with some giants.

subject: Gnonsbim
fact: Gnonsbim is the Captain of the Guard of Sheernobb and is running for re-election. He has sent adventurers to investigate bandits to appear proactive, though the real threat is giants. He is romantically interested in Pasmarie Clee, and his actions are politically motivated.
source_quote: He’s running for re-election and wants to show he’s a man of action.

subject: Pasmarie Clee
fact: Pasmarie Clee is the keeper of Sheernobb’s finest beehives. Her honey shipment bound for Verbobonc was stolen by raiders who speak of the 'Black Earth' and wield stone weapons. She cannot pursue them herself but offers enchanted honey as reward. She is practical, resilient, and deeply invested in her village’s reputation.
source_quote: This honey isn’t just about trade. It carries Sheernobb’s name and our reputation. If we lose the trust of the merchants, our village will suffer.

subject: Black Earth
fact: The Black Earth is a mysterious cult or faction responsible for raiding Pasmarie’s honey caravans. They wield stone weapons and speak of ancient, earth-bound ideologies. Their presence suggests a deeper, possibly magical or heretical movement operating in the Kron Hills.
source_quote: The attackers weren’t bandits—no, they spoke of the ‘Black Earth’ and carried weapons of stone.

subject: honey theft
fact: A caravan carrying Pasmarie Clee’s enchanted honey to Verbobonc was ambushed on the trade road north of Sheernobb. The attackers, linked to the Black Earth, stole the cargo and vanished into the Kron Hills, threatening the village’s economic and cultural standing.
source_quote: The caravan was ambushed on the trade road just north of the village.

subject: Sheernobb
fact: Sheernobb is a village in the Kron Hills, known for its beehives, enchanted honey, and political tensions between its Headgnome, Captain of the Guard, and local artisans. It is culturally significant as a crossroads of trade and tradition, with a moot hall where governance occurs.
source_quote: You are in the moot hall of Sheernobb, one of my clan villages in this part of the Kron Hills.

subject: Pasmarie’s Beehives
fact: Pasmarie’s Beehives are a well-maintained farmstead southeast of Sheernobb, surrounded by verdant fields and wildflowers. The hives are arranged in neat rows, and the area serves as both a productive asset and a symbol of Sheernobb’s identity. A small building with a wooden doorway serves as her workshop and meeting space.
source_quote: The hives are neatly arranged in rows, with the buzzing of bees creating a harmonious backdrop.

subject: Gnarley Forest
fact: The Gnarley Forest is a vast, ecologically rich woodland spanning multiple regions including Verbobonc, Dyvers, the Domain of Greyhawk, and the Kron Hills. It is a cultural and magical crossroads, home to Sylvan Elves, treants, unicorns, and ancient secrets. Its glades and valleys conceal hidden paths and forgotten lore.
source_quote: A sprawling woodland straddling the borders of Verbobonc, Viscounty, Dyvers, the Domain of Greyhawk, the Wild Coast, Celene, and the Kron Hills...

subject: enchanted honey
fact: The enchanted honey of Sheernobb is a rare magical substance produced by Pasmarie’s bees. It possesses restorative properties capable of saving lives in peril. It is the village’s most prized export and a symbol of its prestige, stolen by the Black Earth raiders.
source_quote: You’ll have my gratitude and a share of my finest enchanted honey—a taste of Sheernobb’s magic that might save your life in a pinch.

subject: map with annotations
fact: A map purchased by Zephyr has been annotated by Pasmarie Clee to mark the location of the honey caravan ambush. It now includes a northeastward trail leading into the Gnarley Forest, where further clues may lie. Additional notes on the map describe the forest’s ecological and mystical significance.
source_quote: She marks it. 'It had happened a few miles to the north east.'

subject: weasel
fact: A weasel appeared suddenly in Glennddarc’s lap, waking him with a grouchy yelp. It nuzzled his ear, flipped onto its back, and bared its soft underbelly. It is unusually tame and appears to have a strange, almost sentient bond with the Headgnome, suggesting possible magical influence or familiar status.
source_quote: The weasel darts quickly to nuzzle the elder's ear, then flips on its back, baring its soft underbelly.

subject: old woman in Gnarley Forest
fact: An old woman in a brown dress, green woolen shirt, and leather belt appears in a glade of the Gnarley Forest. She greets Zephyr with unnatural familiarity. Her appearance is subtly wrong — perhaps enchanted, disguised, or a manifestation of the forest’s ancient magic. Her presence suggests a hidden guardian, spirit, or trap.
source_quote: There is something off about her.

subject: Planting 21, 579 Late Afternoon
fact: On this date, Zephyr and his companions arrive at Pasmarie’s Beehives and learn of the honey theft. The event marks the beginning of their investigation into the Black Earth raiders.
source_quote: Planting 21, 579 Late Afternoon

subject: Planting 22, 579
fact: The following day, Zephyr receives guidance from the half-orc cook Quinna Poul regarding the boar in the Gnarley Forest. He enters the forest and encounters the mysterious old woman, deepening the mystery.
source_quote: Planting 22, 579

subject: the chest
fact: Zephyr believes that finding the stolen honey is linked to locating 'the chest' — an object of greater value or significance. The chest may contain more than just honey — perhaps relics, documents, or magical artifacts tied to the Black Earth or Sheernobb’s hidden history.
source_quote: Reward is added to the other reward. And we get to find the chest.

subject: the old woman's identity
fact: The old woman in the Gnarley Forest greets Zephyr with uncanny familiarity. Her attire, demeanor, and unnatural presence suggest she is not merely a hermit — she may be a spirit, a druid, a fey entity, or a magical construct tied to the forest’s ancient magic.
source_quote: There is something off about her.

subject: Aunt Emma
fact: Aunt Emma is a green hag who disguised herself as an old woman to lure travelers to her gingerbread house, where she planned to fatten and eat them. She was killed by Zephyr after her true form was revealed.
source_quote: I am just an old lady who has a thing for making sweets and fattening up travelers! It’s a joy that I have.

subject: Green Hag
fact: A green hag, formerly disguised as Aunt Emma, attacked Zephyr and Zinnia in her gingerbread house. Her appearance was an illusion; her true form had green skin, green eyes, clawed hands, and sharp teeth. She pleaded for her life after realizing she might not survive, but was killed by Zephyr.
source_quote: Let me live, and I will tell you where my treasure is!

subject: Hat of Wizardry
fact: Found by Zinnia near the hag’s oven, this magical hat can be sold or shared with Spugnoir. It was among the hag’s loot.
source_quote: He finds a hat of Wizardry, which he thinks can be sold or shared with Spugnoir.

subject: The Hag's Guide to 101 Recipes Of Children
fact: A darkly themed book found on the floor near the oven, detailing recipes for children. It confirms the hag’s predatory nature and was taken by Zinnia.
source_quote: He notices a book on the floor near the oven—'The Hag's Guide to 101 Recipes Of Children.'

subject: Plum Pie
fact: The pie baked by the hag is poisonous. Zinnia sniffed it and realized its danger, but chose to eat the gingerbread instead.
source_quote: He takes a sniff of the pie and realizes it is poisonous.

subject: Gingerbread House
fact: A single-room dwelling constructed entirely of gingerbread, with white frosting window trim, sugared plum roof decorations, and a wood oven. It was the lair of the green hag.
source_quote: The walls and roof are made of gingerbread. The window trim is made of white frosting... The roof fascia is decorated with white frosting and what appear to be sugared plums.

subject: Wild Boar
fact: A magnificent boar encountered in a glade, described as matching Quinna Poul’s account. It was successfully tricked into submission by Zinnia’s illusion after Zephyr’s attempt failed.
source_quote: The boar is as magnificent as Quinna Poul said and is eating the grass of the glade.

subject: Bronze Wood Glade
fact: A glade surrounded by bronze wood trees with slender trunks, reddish-brown hard bark, and branches growing at 45-degree angles with 8-inch leaves. The trees are nearly 40 feet tall, evoking Zinnia’s childhood memories.
source_quote: The trees around the glade are bronze wood trees... almost 40 feet above ground... a branch, growing at a natural 45-degree angle to the trunk with 8-inch leaves sprouting from it.

subject: Dryad’s Glade
fact: A glade containing a solitary tree and a sad, humanoid dryad with branches on its arms and leaves on its head. The dryad was weeping over a stolen barrel, believing its beloved had rejected it.
source_quote: This time, a solitary tree is in the middle of the tall grass. Near the tree is a strange creature... The beast looks sad as it stares at a barrel.

subject: Dryad
fact: A sorrowful dryad who stole a barrel, believing it belonged to her beloved. She was convinced by Zephyr that stealing was wrong and that drinking required permission, not theft.
source_quote: She doesn’t love me!... I was just so upset.

subject: Quinna Poul
fact: A delighted patron who promised a grand feast on the 30th of the month after Zinnia delivered the wild boar. She also promised a feast for Zephyr and Zinnia's companions.
source_quote: Yes! I will throw the most fantastic feast on the 30th of this month! And I promised a feast for you and your friends.

subject: Glennon Clee
fact: A man who asked Zinnia if he found his stolen barrels. Zinnia initially said no, then agreed to retrieve them. He later showed Zinnia the trail where the barrels were taken.
source_quote: Did you find my barrels?... Will you?... Yes.

subject: Barrels
fact: Stolen barrels, originally belonging to Glennon Clee, were taken by the dryad. Zinnia tracked them to the dryad’s glade and witnessed the theft’s emotional cause.
source_quote: Zinnia looks at the footprints... Easy trail... The dryad stares at a barrel.

subject: Treasure of the Hag
fact: The green hag claimed to know the location of her treasure, but Zephyr refused to listen. The treasure’s whereabouts remain unknown, and Zinnia searched the house without finding it.
source_quote: Let me live, and I will tell you where my treasure is!... Zephyr will have none of that and kills her.

subject: Barrel Theft Motive
fact: The dryad stole the barrel out of emotional despair, believing her beloved had abandoned her. The theft was not malicious, but born of loneliness, and was resolved through Zephyr’s moral reasoning.
source_quote: I was told when humans are dumped, they drink... I didn’t want to steal. I was just so upset.

subject: Zinnia’s Vengeance
fact: Zinnia has long wanted to kill a hag after childhood stories of hags eating children. He felt relief and vengeance after the hag’s death, fulfilling a personal arc.
source_quote: I have wanted to kill a hag since I heard the stories from my mother about hags that ate little children... He feels the relief of getting vengeance on the terrors of a child.

subject: Feast on the 30th
fact: Quinna Poul promised a grand feast on the 30th of the current month, following the delivery of the wild boar. It is an upcoming event tied to Zinnia’s success.
source_quote: I will throw the most fantastic feast on the 30th of this month!

subject: Hag’s Death
fact: Zephyr killed the green hag after she revealed her true form and pleaded for her life. He refused her offer to reveal her treasure’s location.
source_quote: Zephyr will have none of that and kills her.

subject: Boar’s Capture
fact: Zinnia successfully tricked the wild boar using an illusion after Zephyr’s attempt failed. The boar was then delivered to Quinna Poul.
source_quote: Zephyr’s attempt at an illusion doesn’t trick the boar, but Zinnia’s does... Zinnia stands with the boar next to Quinna.

subject: Dryad’s Redemption
fact: Zephyr convinced the dryad that stealing was wrong and that drinking required permission. The dryad abandoned her theft and expressed sorrow, not malice.
source_quote: Zephyr explains that the barrel wasn’t his for the taking... The dryad... declares, 'Well, I didn’t want to steal. I was just so upset.'

subject: Hags
fact: Hags are predatory creatures known for luring travelers to their lairs, often disguised as harmless old women, and consuming them. The green hag’s actions confirm this pattern.
source_quote: She’s a hag... I am just an old lady who has a thing for making sweets and fattening up travelers!

subject: Zinnia’s Perception of Truth
fact: Zinnia insists on seeing beyond appearances — recognizing the hag’s disguise, the dryad’s sorrow, and the true nature of the barrel theft. He is the one who names the truth others miss.
source_quote: She’s a hag... He notices that something is off. She is not who she says she is.
